{{Short description|French mathematician (1941–2014)}}
{{for|the artist|Louis-Maurice Boutet de Monvel}}
[[File:Louis Boutet de Monvel Oberwolfach 2011.jpg|thumb|Boutet de Monvel at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2011]]
'''Louis Boutet de Monvel''' (22 June 1941 – 25 December 2014) was a French mathematician who worked on [[functional analysis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://smf.emath.fr/content/d%C3%A9c%C3%A8s-de-louis-boutet-de-monvel|title=Décès de Louis Boutet de Monvel|publisher=smf.emath.fr|date=25 December 2014|language=French|access-date=30 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228223412/http://smf.emath.fr/content/d%C3%A9c%C3%A8s-de-louis-boutet-de-monvel|archive-date=28 December 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was a student of  [[Laurent Schwartz]] in [[Paris]] and was professor at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]]. He was married to [[Anne Boutet de Monvel]], also a mathematician.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Simon | first = Barry
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-030-22422-6
 | isbn = 978-3-030-22421-9
 | mr = 3969971
 | page = 357
 | publisher = Springer, Cham
 | series = Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften [Fundamental Principles of Mathematical Sciences]
 | title = Loewner's theorem on monotone matrix functions
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=hSmsDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA357
 | volume = 354
 | year = 2019| url-access = subscription
 }}</ref>

In 2007, he was awarded the [[Émile Picard Medal]] of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and in 2003 the [[Prix de l'État]].

According to the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]
<ref>Louis Boutet de Monvel at the [https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=66526 Mathematics Genealogy Project], October 2021.</ref> 
his Ph.D. students are 
AbdelAli Attioui (1994), Jean-Marc Delort, 
[[Bernard Helffer]] (1976), 
[[Gilles Lebeau]] (1984), 
[[George Marinescu (mathematician)|George Marinescu]] (1994), 
[[Philibert Nang]] (1996), 	
Serge Lukasiewicz (1997), 
Alexander Rezounenko (1997).
